observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: The body is MOV EAX,[imm32] ; RET. It reads no register at all, takes no stack argument and returns with a bare RET, so the compiled bytes are identical under __cdecl, __stdcall, __thiscall and __fastcall. 32 observed callsites all pass no argument and none adjusts ESP, which is consistent with every convention. No convention is claimed.

observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x00b3d290: MOV EAX,[0x0167EAD4] is the only write to EAX, so all 32 bits are defined and no truncation or zero-extension occurs.
observed_original_abi.hidden_this_register: ECX is never read; the body contains no register operand other than EAX in the MOV and the implicit ESP in the RET

semantic_contract: The function is a pure accessor: it returns the 32-bit contents of one fixed .bss cell, 0x0167EAD4, and does nothing else. It has no inputs, no branches, no callees, no side effects and no frame. It is total - it never fails, never blocks and never allocates. It does not null-check and does not lazily construct, so before the owning subsystem initialises it returns 0. The cell has no static writer in the binary, so its value is installed at runtime; every observed caller passes the result straight into ECX as a this pointer, and one caller (0x00ac5330) explicitly null-checks it first, which establishes that the cell holds a pointer-sized handle to a runtime-installed object. The 32-call fan-in and the uniform CALL/MOV ECX,EAX shape identify it as a widely used singleton accessor, but nothing read from the binary names the object it returns.
classification_rationale: The complete body, ABI, the single global, its observed value, the absence of a static writer and the receiver-shaped use at every inspected callsite are all read directly from the binary, so the behaviour is established with no uncertainty. What is bounded is the identity of the pointee: no instruction inside the function touches it, no static writer names it, no vtable was located for it, and no SDK declaration could be matched without contradicting observed field usage. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld because the owning type is a material element and it is not established; STRUCTURAL_ONLY is too weak because a complete behavioural claim is supported.
semantic_findings: 0x00b3d290 is exactly `return *(uint32_t*)0x0167EAD4;` - two instructions, six bytes, one global, no control flow.
The result is a runtime-installed singleton handle: 32 callsites, and every inspected one is CALL 0x00b3d290 ; MOV ECX,EAX ; CALL <method>.

0x0167EAD4 has no static writer anywhere in the binary (single xref, a READ from this function), so it is populated by runtime initialisation, not by a static initialiser table that Ghidra could name.
The function is total: no null check, no lazy construction, no error path. Before initialisation it returns 0, and the one caller that null-checks proves that 0 is an expected value.

The function sits in a run of fifteen sibling accessors over the consecutive .bss block 0x0167EAC0..0x0167EAEC, but that run is NOT homogeneous: 0x00b3d220 returns an address rather than a value, 0x00b3d2c0 is a type-id demultiplexer, and 0x00b3d2f0 is a thiscall forwarder. Block adjacency therefore supports 'one of a family of Simulator singleton accessors' and nothing more specific.
unresolved_questions: What object does 0x0167EAD4 point to at runtime? No vtable was located for it and no instruction in the binary names it. This is the material bound on this record.
Which runtime code writes 0x0167EAD4? There is no static writer and no DATA xref, so the writer is reached through a pointer, a registration table, or a runtime patch that Ghidra cannot attribute.

Is 0x0167EAD4 the same type as the neighbouring slot 0x0167EAD8 (read by 0x00b3d260, whose pointee is dereferenced through vtable slot +0x30 at 0x00b32ad0)? The two accessors are adjacent but nothing observed relates the two pointees.

CONFLICT, recorded and NOT adopted: Spore-ModAPI 'Spore ModAPI/Spore/Simulator/SubSystem/GamePersistenceManager.h:65' declares `DeclareAddress(Get);  // 0xB3D2A0 0xB3D440`, and 0x00b3d290 falls inside that range. The attribution is not adopted because 0x00b3d2a0, the range's stated entry point, demonstrably returns an object read at +0x184 (ordered map header, 0x00bb99fc) and at +0x1F4 (lazily resolved pointer slot, 0x00c4b221), while the same header asserts ASSERT_SIZE(cGamePersistenceManager, 0x4C). The SDK's address range therefore covers a cluster of unrelated Simulator singleton accessors, and only 0x00b3d2a0 is claimed by name. Adopting cGamePersistenceManager for 0x00b3d290 would contradict an observed field offset.

The briefing's canonical ledger recorded caller_count 32; the live xref query finds 37 call sites across 33 distinct caller functions, because several callers call it more than once. The fan-in figure is not a contradiction, only a different counting convention.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has ever been captured for this function; the original Cell stage has never been entered in any recorded run. Every claim here is static.
A runtime differential test would have to establish (a) that 0x0167EAD4 is non-zero once the owning subsystem is up, and (b) the concrete type of the pointee, which is the withheld claim.
Because the slot has no static writer, static analysis alone cannot enumerate the set of objects that can land there; a runtime write watchpoint on 0x0167EAD4 is the only way to close this.
